itinerary.cal: Camp falls within a North Cascades NP cross-country/high-occupancy zone requiring a backcountry permit — reserve ahead for summer weekends.

days.note: Hike the Hannegan Pass Trail (4 miles) to the pass, then leave trail to climb open heather and snow slopes of the Ruth Arm to a high camp around 6,600 ft below the Ruth-Icy col. Mountaineers guidance is to camp on snow where possible to minimize impact.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near the Ruth Arm / Ruth-Icy col

days.note: Break camp and climb the short remaining glacier slope to Ruth's summit, then follow the connecting ridge to Icy Peak, including one short pitch of low-5th/exposed scrambling near its summit block. After tagging Icy, reverse the traverse back over the col and descend all the way out to the trailhead — a long day. Very fit parties occasionally link both summits car-to-car in one push instead of camping.
days.title: Traverse Ruth Mountain to Icy Peak and out

schedule.label: Top out Ruth Mountain
schedule.detail: 7,115 ft; stash overnight gear near the col if not carrying over.

schedule.label: Cross Ruth-Icy col
schedule.detail: Begin Icy Peak's summit block, one short pitch of easy technical ground.

schedule.label: Summit Icy Peak
schedule.detail: ~7,073 ft (the true, slightly-higher SE point sits about 11 ft above the peak most maps label as the top).

days.objective: Climb Ruth Mountain, traverse to and summit Icy Peak, then descend fully to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, ~16.5-mile trip with roughly 8,000 cumulative ft of gain (and a matching ~8,000 ft of loss): most parties camp near the Ruth-Icy col and make one long day tagging both summits before descending fully to the trailhead.

before.approach: Shares its trailhead and lower approach with the South Slopes/Ruth Glacier route: Hannegan Pass Trail #674 from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of FR-32) up the Ruth Creek valley to Hannegan Pass (5,066 ft, ~4 miles, ~2,000 ft gain), then the climbers' path east and south past the pond below the pass (faint, easy to lose), around a cliff-band shoulder, and onto the Ruth Glacier's north slope to a camp near the notch northwest of Ruth's summit (~6,600 ft) — see the South Slopes route for full trailhead-to-glacier detail, including the documented crevasse-fall hazard on the lower glacier despite its mellow appearance. From camp, the traverse is conventionally done Ruth-to-Icy: tag Ruth's summit first, then descend roughly 800 ft south and west toward a gully on the peak's west side, pick up a faint boot path, and continue down another ~800 ft (about 1,600 ft total off Ruth's summit) to the low saddle/col between Ruth and Icy at roughly 6,600-6,800 ft. Parties choose between a steeper, more direct 'death gully' line or supposedly-cairned heather slopes and game trails to climber's left holding 2nd-3rd class ground — the heather-slope option is the safer, recommended line. From the saddle, cross a patch of trees and talus/boot-path along the connecting ridge to the Icy Glacier, then ascend talus and slabs below a rock ridge to gain the glacier proper, aiming for a notch/saddle just west of Icy's Northwest Spire (~6,500 ft). From that notch it's another ~500 ft of 2nd-3rd class scrambling up an obvious left-hand, light-colored gully system to the base of Icy's summit block, where a 100-ft, 4th-class gully (solid jugs and ledges but real exposure) leads to the top. Helmets are standard here given loose rock and traffic funneled through a single gully. Note the true (highest) summit is the SE point, about 11 ft higher than the peak most maps label as the top.

Parties choose between a steeper, more direct 'death gully' line or supposedly-cairned heather slopes and game trails to climber's left holding 2nd-3rd class ground — the heather-slope option is the safer, recommended line.

climbing_route.label: Light-colored gully system to the summit block

approach_variants.name: Hannegan Pass and Ruth Mountain first, then down to the Ruth-Icy saddle and across to the Icy Glacier
approach_variants.notes:
Shares its trailhead and lower approach with the Ruth Glacier route: Trail #674 from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead up Ruth Creek to Hannegan Pass at 5,066 ft, then the faint climbers' path east and south past the pond, around the cliff-band shoulder, and onto the Ruth Glacier's north slope to a camp near the notch northwest of Ruth's summit around 6,600 ft.

The traverse is conventionally done Ruth-to-Icy: tag Ruth's summit first, then descend roughly 800 ft south and west toward a gully on the peak's west side, pick up a faint boot path, and continue down another 800 ft or so — about 1,600 ft in total off Ruth's summit — to the low saddle between Ruth and Icy at roughly 6,600-6,800 ft.

From the saddle, cross a patch of trees and follow talus and boot path along the connecting ridge to the Icy Glacier, then talus and slabs below a rock ridge to gain the glacier proper.

The re-ascent of Ruth on the way home is the sting in the tail and cannot be avoided on the standard car-to-car version.
hazards: A steep loose 'death gully' that is the natural fall line off Ruth and the wrong line
A long horizontal crevasse near the top of the Icy Glacier below the towers
A bergschrund near the west notch in some seasons
Loose rock funnelled through a single summit gully with the whole party in it
Roughly 1,600-2,000 ft of re-ascent over Ruth on the way home, at the end of a twelve-hour day
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE DECISION THAT MATTERS IS WHICH LINE YOU TAKE OFF RUTH, AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. There are two ways down the 1,600 ft to the Ruth-Icy saddle: a steeper, more direct gully that parties call the death gully, and cairned heather slopes and game trails to CLIMBER'S LEFT holding second and third class ground. Take the HEATHER, on the left. The direct gully is the one you will drift into if you simply point downhill, which is what makes this worth stating rather than assuming.

ARRIVAL AT THE SADDLE: it is the LOW POINT between the two peaks, around 6,600-6,800 ft, and there are trees in it. Trees are the confirmation — you have dropped below the alpine on both sides. If you are still on open snow or talus with nothing growing, you have not reached the saddle.

THE NOTCH WEST OF THE NORTHWEST SPIRE IS THE BASE OF THE CLIMBING, at about 6,500 ft. From the saddle, cross the connecting ridge to the Icy Glacier and aim for a notch or saddle just WEST of Icy's Northwest Spire. Watch for a long horizontal crevasse near the top of the glacier below the Icy towers, and for a bergschrund near the notch in some seasons.

THE SUMMIT GULLY IS THE FINAL TEST AND IT IS UNAMBIGUOUS. From the notch, about 500 ft of second and third class up an obvious LEFT-HAND, LIGHT-COLOURED gully system reaches the base of the summit block. The climbing is a single 100 ft fourth-class gully with solid jugs and ledges, real exposure, and rappel slings around a horn at its top. Take the FIRST PROMINENT GULLY. Sling anchors at the top of a 100 ft gully are the arrival marker; if there is nothing at the top and the gully keeps going, you are in the wrong one.

AND THE ONE THAT CATCHES PEOPLE AT THE VERY END: the true high point is the SOUTHEAST point, about 11 ft higher than the peak most maps label as the top. The register is on the northwest summit. Decide before you leave the notch which one you are going to.

sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Traverse Ruth Mountain to Icy Peak and out

before.descent_text: From Icy's summit block, most parties rappel the crux 4th-class gully rather than downclimb it: there is a solid boulder/horn at the top used as a natural anchor — no bolts or fixed gear are reported on this route. Trip reports split between a single ~30m rappel that covers just the hardest, most exposed section (with easy 2nd/3rd-class downclimbing below) and a single full-length rappel with a 60m rope that gets the whole gully done in one shot. Plan on 1 rappel total; bring at least a 30m single or 60m rope so you have the option to skip the downclimb entirely. There is no other technical rappelling on the route. Below the gully, reverse the 2nd-3rd class terrain and talus back down to the Icy Glacier notch, cross back to the Ruth-Icy saddle, and climb back up and over Ruth's south/west slopes (re-gaining roughly the 1,600 ft descended earlier) to the notch/camp area northwest of Ruth's summit — there's no way to avoid this re-ascent on the standard car-to-car traverse. From there, reverse the South Slopes/Ruth Glacier descent: down the glacier's moderate but crevassed north slope, along the climbers' path past the pond below Hannegan Pass, and out Trail #674 down the Ruth Creek valley to the trailhead. Total round trip is roughly 16 miles with on the order of 8,000 cumulative ft of gain including the up-and-over of Ruth on the return; trip reports cite around 12 hours of moving time from camp, so most parties treat this as a long single push from a Ruth-area camp rather than a car-to-car day.

pitch_detail.grade: 4th class (some parties find it feels low 5th)
pitch_detail.notes: Solid jugs and ledges with real exposure; most parties rappel this pitch rather than downclimb it.
pitch_detail.anchor: Natural rock horn/boulder at the top of the gully; no bolts or fixed gear reported

before.bail: The traverse has no fixed rappel stations; retreat before committing to the Icy Peak gully is straightforward by reversing the glacier/talus traverse back over the saddle to Ruth's summit and down the Ruth Glacier to Hannegan Pass. Past the saddle, the short summit gully on Icy is the route's only real commitment point and can usually be downclimbed.
gear: 2-3 snow pickets and a crevasse-rescue kit for the Ruth Glacier portion
Climbing helmet (mandatory — active rockfall on Icy)
Harness plus a few slings/rap rings or tat for an optional rappel off Icy's summit gully
30m+ rope is adequate for a single-strand rappel of the ~100 ft gully
rack: 2-3 snow pickets and crevasse-rescue kit for the Ruth Glacier crossing
Harness plus slings/rap rings or tat for an optional rappel of Icy's summit gully (~100ft, single strand)

partner_requirements.fitnessSpec: Fit for a ~15.5-hour remote day with a loaded pack
requiredSkills: Sustained exposed 2nd-4th class ridge/talus scrambling beyond Ruth's summit with real route-finding (faint boot path to Icy's NW Spire notch)
A short low-5th move near the notch
Good weather judgment — exposed, shelterless saddle/ridge with serious retreat once past the saddle
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid glacier travel/crevasse rescue for the Ruth Glacier ascent — not a place to learn
